newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean banks to supply 44.7 bln won to Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean banks to supply 44.7 bln won to Hanbo.

text.p: South Korean creditor banks will supply 44.7 billion won in emergency funds to keep the debt-stricken Hanbo Steel Co running, the Ministry of Finance and Economy said on Thursday.
A ministry statement said it expected a Seoul court to grant receivership to Hanbo Steel, South Koreas's second largest steelmaker, next week.
"The emergency funds are intended to help Hanbo's operation until the receivership is allowed," said a ministry official. Hanbo had asked for 129.7 bilion won in such funds, he added.
Hanbo filed for court protection from creditors on Tuesday after piling up more than five trillion won of loans from 61 banks and financial institutions.
Hanbo's creditors have already said they will suspend demands for debt repayments and resume overdraft facilities with Hanbo once the receivership is given.
The ministry said it had asked Korea Electric Power Corp and gas supplier Yukong Ltd to keep providing energy to Hanbo Steel, which defaulted on debt repayments last week.
The ministry also said it would grant tax benefits to Hanbo's suppliers and sub-contractors to help relieve a financial squeeze.
